baseline.delta_vs_previous: +166.9% (2,918,112 -> 7,789,333). SEE metric_caveat -- this delta is an accounting artifact, not a real regression.

metric_caveat.summary: 4 of the 10 sampled sessions ran on a non-Anthropic backend (model 'deepseek-v4-pro'). On those sessions input_tokens = 95,801,342 and cache_read_input_tokens = 93,280,128 -- near-identical, indicating that backend reports TOTAL prompt tokens in input_tokens while ALSO reporting cache reads separately. reflection_metrics.py sums both, so cached input is counted twice. The 6 Anthropic sessions show input_tokens = 12,008 against cache_read_input_tokens = 113,369,212, i.e. cleanly non-overlapping, which is the contrast that proves the double-count.
metric_caveat.corrected_estimate: Removing the 93,280,128 overlap gives ~23,559,867 billed tokens over 15 completed issues = ~1,570,658 tokens/issue, i.e. roughly -46% vs the 2026-07-22 baseline rather than +167%. Treat as an estimate, not a measurement.
metric_caveat.note: No fix proposed: scripts/reflection_metrics.py is outside this loop's permitted optimization surface. Recommend a separate issue to make the script backend-aware (e.g. drop input_tokens from the billed sum when it is within a few percent of cache_read_input_tokens, or record the backend per session).

evidence.quote: t189 'On branch master' -> t196 commit made on master -> t201 gh pr create fails: 'you must first push the current branch to a remote' -> t213 'git push origin master' SUCCEEDS: 'efd8856..fa7edf7 master -> master' -> t219 'head branch "master" is the same as base branch "master", cannot create a pull request' -> t224 'I see the commit was pushed directly to master. Let me create a proper PR by reverting this' -> t228 'git push origin master --force' -> t231 branch created and work redone.

proposals.diff_summary: governance.md's PR-merge-gate item 2 said 'No direct pushes to master ... Branch protection enforces this; do not try to bypass it.' The transcript proves branch protection does NOT block it -- the push to master succeeded, and the recovery required a force-push of master. The false assurance made the rule read as something the platform guarantees rather than something the agent must actively do, and it was stated as a merge-gate principle with no action attached at the moment it matters (before the first commit). Replaced with a truthful statement that nothing blocks the push, plus a concrete pre-commit check (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD, branch if it says master), an explanation of why committing first and branching after is not equivalent, and an explicit prohibition on force-pushing master.
proposals.expected_impact: The observed incident cost ~50 turns of pure rework (t188-t237) including a rewritten history on the shared master branch. Prevents recurrence of a governance breach whose cost is not primarily tokens. Adds ~9 lines to a file loaded once per session that already gets read before the first GitHub operation; net token cost is negligible against one avoided incident.

t32 'I am worried about three things that I would like your support with. - Edge tab ... - Promotion tab - I had 1 station flagged for promotion but yesterday ...' -- a third independent health/anomaly triage request.

proposals.diff_summary: Health-report and production-bug triage is the single most common session shape in this batch (5 of 10 transcripts: 109569e8, 4a846eee, a37abffa, b25b5aae, 9b6c1152) and had no procedural surface at all -- every session re-derived how to reach the DB and the logs from scratch. Across the batch this produced 43 hand-written sqlite3.connect blocks and 12 separate bot.log scans, with inconsistent read-only discipline and a five-pass window escalation on a 100 MB+ log. Adds a health-triage skill capturing: graphify-and-git-log orientation before probing (a changed metric usually tracks a merge), the read-only DB connection idiom, the seek-from-end log idiom with window sizing, a verify-before-filing checklist whose counter-check step targets the exact failure that produced the t241 retraction (a metric at 0.0% or at a bound is more often an unfireable threshold or saturated clamp than a fixed bug), and grouping by root cause rather than symptom. Registered in pm.md's skill-routing table and CLAUDE.md's skill list.
proposals.expected_impact: Skill body is ~85 lines and loads only when invoked, so it costs nothing on epic-execution sessions. Against the observed pattern it should remove the ~4 wasted bot.log passes per health session (each returning multi-MB grep output into context) and the per-query sqlite boilerplate rewrite, and -- the larger win -- prevent at least one wrong-root-cause issue per report, which in 109569e8 cost a filed issue, a public retraction comment, a re-scope, and a relabel. Conservatively 10k-30k tokens per health session plus one avoided correction cycle.

evidence.quote: t552 Agent spawn 'dev-861'. t561 user: 'lets pause'. t563 assistant: '#861 - dev-861 is running in the background on the boundary-convention fix; I'll get a notification when it finishes'. t566 user: 'stop the spawned agent, i had requested this already'. t573 TaskStop(dev-861). t577 'Apologies for missing that the first time. Since it was mid-work (had gotten as far as running tests), the board item for #861 is likely still sitting in whatever state the agent...'

proposals.diff_summary: pm.md's behavioural rules say nothing about in-flight subagents when the user pauses. On 'lets pause' the PM stopped issuing new work but left a spawned mid-dev running and reported it as such, requiring an explicit second user instruction to kill it -- and by then the agent had run far enough to leave the board mid-transition. Adds a rule that pause/stop/hold-off covers work already in flight: TaskStop every running subagent first, report what was stopped and where it got to, then reconcile the board for any issue whose agent was killed mid-transition.
proposals.expected_impact: Removes one user correction turn plus the TaskStop round-trip per pause, and avoids board state diverging from reality when an agent is killed mid-transition (which the PM then has to detect and repair). Adds ~7 lines to pm.md, loaded once per PM session.

evidence.quote: Session-level usage totals, model 'deepseek-v4-pro': input_tokens=54,173,508 alongside cache_read_input_tokens=53,285,632 -- the two track each other across all 4 deepseek sessions (95,801,342 vs 93,280,128 in aggregate), while the 6 Anthropic sessions show 12,008 vs 113,369,212.

proposals.diff_summary: JSON-ONLY, NO DIFF -- scripts/reflection_metrics.py is explicitly outside this loop's optimization surface, so this is recorded for a human to action as a normal issue. The tokens-per-completed-issue metric double-counts cached input on non-Anthropic backends, which made this run report +166.9% when the like-for-like figure is closer to -46%. Until fixed, the convergence metric is not comparable across runs that mix backends.
proposals.expected_impact: No token impact. Restores the trustworthiness of the one number this whole loop is supposed to converge; without it, future reflection runs will chase phantom regressions.

considered_and_rejected.topic: A dedicated health-check / bug-detection subagent (user question for this run)
considered_and_rejected.verdict: Rejected in favour of P2 (a skill). Not overkill as a workload -- 5 of 10 sessions -- but wrong shape as an agent. The diagnostic value in 109569e8 came from holding the DB, the logs, the source and the git history in one context and cross-referencing them (t46-t72 log+DB, t171-t233 source+DB, t269-t301 parser+bracket_evals), which is exactly what a cold-start subagent cannot do; it would re-pay the context load and return a summary the PM must independently re-verify anyway -- a habit this PM already exercises against dev agents (t458, t538, t664 all re-run the agent's own tests). The output is also issue creation plus board transitions, which governance assigns to the PM. The one genuinely fan-out-shaped part, read-only evidence sweeps, is already served by the existing Explore agent. Revisit only if health triage starts needing to run concurrently with epic execution rather than as its own session.
